study.name: Dysbiotic synthetic gut community
study.description: A 6-species synthetic human gut community was established using the ambr15f fermentation robot. The ambr15f, a high-throughput fermentation robot with two culture stations housing 12 single-use microbioreactors (vessels) each, placed in an anaerobic chamber (A135 Anaerobic workstation with HEPA filter: 10% H2, 10% CO2, 80% N2, 55% humidity), was used for growing the community for 240 hours, without pH control, in an emulated chemostat mode after 4 hours of inoculation.

project.name: Investigating the response of a synthetic human gut community to perturbations

techniques.description: 100 µL of the sample was used for cell counts using Flow Cytometry (FC) with SYBR Green 1 (SG) staining. Dilutions of 1:10 and 1:100 in 0.9% saline was used for the first two time points (0 and 6h) and the later time points (9h onwards) respectively. 25 µL of 1:100 diluted sample was used for total cell counts by FC where cells were stained using only SG.

Absolute abundances obtained by multiplying copy-corrected relative abundances with total cell counts from FC (cells/mL). Unknowns are unclassified/ low quality reads or contamination16S gene copy numbers were extracted from rrnDB, version 5.10. 
16S gene copy numbers used for this study: B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482: 5; B. fragilis NCTC 9343: 6; F. duncaniae: 6; B. hydrogenotrophica DSM 10507: 4; R. intestinalis L1-82: 6; E. coli LF82: 7
The key metabolites were quantified using HPLC. NA refers to peak not integrated (missed in data processing)

experiments.name: No perturbations
experiments.description: Six species grown in microbioreactor in chemostat mode, maintained at 37°C. Chemostat mode started 4 hours after inoculation.
